intro: I build African-language speech systems from a humanities foundation — literature, philology, and linguistics, not a computer-science degree. I design the linguistic framing and the product, and I work with engineering to ship it. Try Murya, then the CV.

evidence.title: MOS Evaluation Protocol
evidence.text: A blind, randomized Mean Opinion Score study (ITU-T P.800-style, 1–5 naturalness scale, real-human-speech anchor) is live and collecting ratings at app.murya.ng/listen. No score is published until each voice clears a floor of 20 ratings — the study is ongoing and results aren't final yet.

evidence.title: 30k Ƙamus Lexicon Provenance
evidence.text: Compiled from C.H. Robinson (1914, Public Domain) and Prof. Paul Newman (1977, authorized research subset). Verified entries are deduplicated, tone-contoured, and phonetically normalized.

evidence.title: What runs offline
evidence.text: Speech synthesis and dictionary lookup run entirely in the browser. Live conversation uses an optional server connection for speech recognition (Faster-Whisper) and responses (Aya 8B).

numbers.footnote: **Dialect Boundary Notice:** Acoustic tuning is calibrated for Standard Kano Hausa (Eastern dialect). Sokoto and Gobirawa acoustic variations are scheduled for Murya v2.

items.title: 1. Local control
items.text: Open weights can be self-hosted, so the tools don’t depend on a proprietary cloud API that could be shut down or paywalled.

items.title: 2. Works offline
items.text: The 30k-entry dictionary and speech synthesis run in the browser, so they work on low bandwidth or none, which is common across the Sahel.

items.title: 3. Cultural pragmatics
items.text: Responses follow Hausa norms of modesty and respect (*Kunya & Girmamawa*) and gendered address, instead of translated Western conversational templates.
